title: Berlin Flat Notice Period - Quick Summary
items: **Three months is not the rule, the third working day is.** § 573c Absatz 1 BGB says notice is admissible at the latest on the **third working day of a calendar month, to the end of the month after next**. Miss that day by one and the tenancy runs a whole extra month.

**In Berlin the third working day is usually not the 3rd.** Saturday counts as a working day (BGH, 27 April 2005, VIII ZR 206/04), Sundays and the ten Berlin public holidays do not. October 2026 lands on **Monday 5 October**, January 2027 on **Tuesday 5 January**. April and July 2027 land on a Saturday, so deliver by the Friday.

**Posting is not arriving.** Notice takes effect when it reaches the landlord. It must be on **paper and signed** (§ 568 BGB), every name on the contract must sign, and an Einwurf-Einschreiben beats a Rückschein letter, which fails if nobody is home to sign.

**A Kündigungsverzicht overrides all of it.** A notice waiver in a form contract may run **four years at most**, counted from signing. While it runs the third working day does nothing for you, and your landlord does not have to accept a Nachmieter.

**The deposit ceiling is three cold rents.** § 551 BGB caps it at three months of Kaltmiete, lets you pay in three instalments, and requires it to sit in a separate account with the interest going to you.

**Damage claims die after six months.** § 548 BGB time-bars the landlord’s claims six months after the flat comes back. Only a reasonable slice held against the final Nebenkosten bill can honestly stay longer.
